summary: Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS, he held positions at the University of Malaya (1961–1968), Newcastle University (~1970–2005), and a visiting professorship at the University of Vienna in 2008.

Dermott Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his BA at Trinity College Dublin (2003), MA at Leiden University (2009), and completed his PhD at UCLA (2018) under the supervision of William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and held the Carmichael Professorship at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Harvard (1926). He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard (~1910–1932), Gujarat University (~1920–1925), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1931).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1925). He held posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at Open University (~2007) and held a post at the University of Chester in 2019.
Di Jiang is a scholar in linguistics, computational linguistics, and Tibetology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, after completing an MA supervised by James Steele.

Diana L. Eck is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD 1976 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), she served as a professor of comparative religion and Indian studies at Harvard from ~1976 to 2024.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE, she worked at TU Berlin, Humboldt, Leipzig, Hamburg, and was appointed Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

Diane A. Lichtenstein completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She held positions as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art (attested 2005).

Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA (2010) under William M. Bodiford and held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College (attested 2010), and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She was a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.
